note: The Leg-Planning Playground's rows (kogaki#1764): a claim set read into one RelationalStructure; the Legs are derived from it by the runner, one per relation the apex reaches, as the Brief derives them, and ask no row (kogaki#1775). A `{{copy:<name>}}` token in a row's `judgment_point` is replaced at run time by the text `copies.<name>` names in another table, from its `opens` words through the first `closes` words after them; a copy whose words are no longer in that table refuses the Trial before any Call.

sme_read_set.note: Stage 1 (kogaki#1764, kogaki#1766): the Mapper's reading, `sme_map_roles`, extended from one sentence to a set of claims. Under the Mapper's bound, MAPPER_CALLS. `reach` and `unreached` are the runner's, derived from `attains_thesis` through `relates`.
sme_read_set.judgment_point: read the claims in the input, `claims`, each with its `id`, as ONE set of relations among Roles, read for the Persona in `persona`. For each Role, give it a `name`, one short snake_case word, and define it in one or two sentences, as its `context`, as a kind of thing in the world of the Persona: an abstraction a claim's object is one instance of, never that object itself, written in the third person and naming no reader, writer or Persona. Name, as its `attributes`, the one-place predicates the claims state of that Role's object, each one short phrase in the claims' own words, or an empty list where they state none, and, as its `claims`, the ids of the claims its text is read from. Name each relation among Roles as one claim states it, as its `holds`: one sentence stating the relation over the Roles, naming none of the claims' objects and giving it a `name`, one short snake_case word, and writing each Role it relates as `{<name>}`, that Role's name in braces, at least once, with `between` naming the Roles it relates by their names and `from` naming the ONE claim id that states it. Every claim states at least one relation. Then name the relations among those relations the claims turn on, as `higher_order`, one or more, each with a `name`, one short snake_case word, `relates` naming by their names two or more relations or higher-order relations it relates, never itself through another, `holds` stating it over the same Roles, each written as `{<name>}`, and `from` naming the claim ids whose text states that connection. Name as `attains_thesis` the name of the ONE higher-order relation that states `thesis` in the input; it alone carries no `from`. A connection no claim states is written only as that one higher-order relation. A relation or claim the higher-order relation that attains the thesis does not reach through `relates` is left out of the article and listed as unreached; it is not refused. Write no `id`: every element's id is minted after this reading (kogaki#1772). Write no `reach` and no `unreached`: they are derived from `attains_thesis`. Answer the RelationalStructure record and nothing else.
sme_read_set.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `roles` -- a non-empty list of `{ "name": <one short snake_case word, unique in the record>, "context": <one or two sentences>, "attributes": [<one short phrase of the claims>, ...], "claims": [<one or more claim ids>] }`; `relations` -- a non-empty list of `{ "name": <one short snake_case word, unique in the record>, "between": [<two or more Role names>], "holds": <one sentence>, "from": <one claim id> }`; `higher_order` -- a non-empty list of `{ "name": <one short snake_case word, unique in the record>, "relates": [<two or more relation or higher-order relation names>], "holds": <one sentence>, "from": [<the claim ids that state it>] }`, the one `attains_thesis` names carrying no `from`; and `attains_thesis` -- one `higher_order` name. No element carries an `id`: the runner mints `r_<n>`, `c_<n>` and `h_<n>` after the reading (kogaki#1772).
sme_read_set.refusal: a key the record, a Role, a relation or a higher-order relation does not declare, or a declared key missing; an element carrying `id`; a `name` that is not one snake_case word or is repeated, or a reference naming nothing; a Role whose `claims` names no claim of the input, and a Role in no relation, refused naming the Role; a relation whose `from` is not one claim id, and a relation whose `holds` does not carry `{<name>}` for a Role its `between` names, refused naming the relation; a `reach` or `unreached` written on the record; a higher-order relation relating fewer than two relations, or a name that is no relation's or higher-order relation's, or relating itself through another, refused naming it; a higher-order relation other than `attains_thesis` whose `from` is empty or names no claim, and an `attains_thesis` carrying `from`, refused naming it; and an `attains_thesis` absent or naming no higher-order relation. A claim no relation is `from` is not refused: it is listed as unreached. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `structure`.
